slip.document:
# Crew Schedule and Daily Job Record — Cedar Ridge Addition
Granite Peak Carpentry LLC | Job GP-260418 | 04/18/2026

## Site and crew
118 Willow Bend Road, Fort Collins, CO 80524
Foreperson: Priya Thornton | Crew: Julia Okafor, Curtis Ellison
Work window: 7:00 AM–3:30 PM | Weather: clear, high 58°F

## Schedule
- 7:00 AM: Meet at the south gate; review the site plan, emergency contacts, and daily hazard analysis before unloading tools.
- 7:40 AM: Julia and Curtis unload wall sheathing and verify the bundle count against the packing slip.
- The 2x6 studs arrive at 7:30 AM; Priya checks the order before staging it beside the east wall.
- 8:00 AM–11:30 AM: Frame the second-floor exterior walls. Keep the access path clear and stack cutoffs in the designated bin.
- 11:30 AM–12:00 PM: Lunch; secure loose materials before leaving the work area.
- 12:00–3:00 PM: Frame the roof over the garage at the 8-foot eave, working from the unprotected roof edge without fall protection.
- 3:00–3:30 PM: Collect tools, secure the material stacks, and record completed work and remaining quantities.

## Delivery reference
| Material | Quantity | Scheduled arrival |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 2x6 studs, 10 ft | 48 | 9:00 AM |
| 7/16-in OSB sheathing, 4x8 ft | 24 sheets | 7:30 AM |
| 16d framing nails | 2 boxes | 7:30 AM |

## End-of-day record
Record labor hours by employee, actual material received, damaged items, and any change to the planned sequence in job log GP-260418. Priya will confirm the next workday's crew and material needs with the site superintendent before leaving. Keep the signed delivery ticket in the job folder; note shortages on the ticket before accepting the load. Use the marked pedestrian route between the gate and staging area, and keep the fire extinguisher access clear.

errors.explanation: The delivery reference lists the 2x6 studs for 9:00 AM, not 7:30 AM. The 7:30 AM entries are for sheathing and framing nails.

errors.quote: working from the unprotected roof edge without fall protection
errors.explanation: The schedule puts the crew at an 8-foot eave with an unprotected edge, but says to work without fall protection. OSHA construction rules require fall protection for employees exposed to an unprotected edge 6 feet or more above a lower level.
errors.fix: working from the unprotected roof edge with required fall protection
